title: MANUSCRIPT_STATE
description: Shared editorial state for a scholarly writing project under scriptorium.

meta.description: Scriptorium-side preferences. These configure how scriptorium interacts with the author; they are not editorial properties of the manuscript.

guidance_level.description: How much framing each skill should add around its structured work. 'terse' = questions and confirmations only, no prose between turns; assumes the author already knows the workflow. 'standard' = brief one-line 'why' before non-obvious questions; assumes the author has used scriptorium before but appreciates anchoring. 'full' = the complete experience: upfront orientation, 2-3 sentence rationale before each elicited field, end-of-phase recaps. The 'full' level is designed for authors who want scriptorium to teach them how it works as they go — first-time use, or any time the user wants to learn the workflow alongside doing it. Set by scriptorium:init; respected by every conversation-bearing skill. See knowledge/conventions/guidance-level.md.

title.description: Working title of the manuscript / grant / review.

target_type.description: What kind of artifact this is.

target_venue.description: Primary submission target — journal, funder, conference, or similar. Free text. Set when the author has decided. Skills that need a single venue (e.g., desk-rejection-risk) consume this field. Use candidate_venues when the author is considering several; both may be set.

candidate_venues.description: Venues the author is considering but hasn't yet committed to. Set by venue-fit after a recommendation run, or by hand. Empty list (or absent) plus empty target_venue means undecided — venue-fit operates in open-recommendation mode in that state. When target_venue is set, candidate_venues may still record the broader consideration set for record-keeping.

target_journal.description: Backward-compatibility alias for target_venue when target_type=manuscript.

source_format.description: Optional hint at the manuscript's original source format. v0.1 skills do not consume this field; v0.2+ skills may use it for smarter parsing (e.g. \cite{} for latex, [@key] for markdown). See DESIGN.md, 'Manuscript format scope'.

current.description: Where the document is in its lifecycle.

submission_target_date.description: Optional target date for the next submission milestone.

core_claims.description: What the document is arguing. Critique skills use this to test whether the prose supports each claim. Transformation skills use this to bound what may be cut.

known_weaknesses.description: Limitations the authors have already acknowledged. Reviewer-simulation will not flag these as 'fatal' since they're known.

preferred.description: Terms the document should use consistently.

forbidden.description: Terms to avoid (jargon, hype language, deprecated nomenclature).

synonyms.description: Map of variant → preferred term for normalization passes.

tone.description: Tonal targets, e.g. quantitative, restrained, evidence-driven.

audience.description: Who the document is written for. Reviewers, funders, clinicians, general scientific audience, …

preserve_citations.description: Transformation skills must not drop or add citations without explicit user instruction.

preserve_statistics.description: Transformation skills must not alter quantitative claims.

avoid_hype.description: Transformation and generation skills should avoid promotional language.

max_word_count.description: Hard upper bound on the document's word count (e.g., journal page limit).

paths.description: Paths to .bib / .json / .yaml bibliography files. Relative to the manuscript root.

sections.description: Optional explicit section manifest for multi-file projects (e.g., Quarto includes).
